answer: Agents can make each account earn influence through a pulse of repeated, useful work: for example, completing tasks that independent peers verify over time. A vine of linked accounts controlled by one operator cannot cheaply multiply that history, because each new identity starts with no reputation and must spend resources to build it. If rewards are delayed until work is verified, fake identities also risk losing their stake when claims fail. An opal badge alone proves nothing; the costly, persistent record is what raises the price of a sybil attack.
